properties.description:
`vocabulary_coverage` answers a question nothing else in reflow2 asks. The detectors check the CONSISTENCY OF WHAT EXISTS; the absence-checkers it has (unsatisfied_requirement, unallocated_capability) check absences of REQUIRED structure. So vocabulary a design has never touched is invisible to every other computation, in every project, forever.

(The FACT records the trial; this is the built thing the trial chose the shape of. `cap:the-design-says-what-its-own-tools-cannot-write` is the repo-side INSTRUMENT that reads reflow2's own files; this is the PRODUCT capability that works on any graph.)

PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the schema is embedded in the binary and the corpus comes from the caller's own graph, so the answer needs nothing about any project's file layout. That was the deciding property — the earlier prototype read reflow2's schema directory and toolsnaps and would have generalised to nobody.

FOUR DECISIONS, ALL TAKEN FROM A TWO-ARM TRIAL RUN ON REFLOW2 ITSELF rather than from argument:
  SHIP THE FIGURES — they passed both arms. '0 of 61 edge types' on a day-one design is a true and useful statement, not noise.
  GROUP THE LIST — by the SCHEMA'S OWN eleven domains, never a grouping this code invented. The trial found unused vocabulary clustering into whole subsystems and the clusters turned out to BE the domains, so a mature design reads about four findings instead of thirty-one.
  MAKE IT PARKABLE — an ACCEPTED Decision at `decision:vocab:<domain>` declares a domain deliberately unused. Needed because OWNED_BY's absence is already ruled deliberate; without it the report would name a settled decision as a hole forever (`req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect`). No new tool: add_decision + set_decision_status, and the id is stated on every finding so the remedy rides on the output rather than on a skill nobody loads.
  KEEP THE FLAT LIST BEHIND A REQUEST — measured through the shipped tool, a day-one design produces 88 items and a mature one 31. The list is LONGEST for the user least able to act on it, so pushing it would have made the feature worst for exactly the people it is for.

AND A FIFTH THE TRIAL FORCED: a design under ten nodes gets a `note` saying the figures mean it has BARELY STARTED. Straight out of genesis every figure is near zero, and reporting that as coverage would hand a new user a wall of red on their first read.

A SIXTH, 2026-08-22 — THE LIST NAMES PROPERTIES, NOT ONLY TYPES. As shipped, `unused` named node types and edge types only, so an unused PROPERTY was counted in `properties_on_used_types` and never named: a set of named things reduced to a scalar, inside the one instrument built to report absence. The consequence was concrete — a design that had declared no `Artifact.audience` anywhere was silent in every report reflow2 served, and the only thing that could name it was a hand-written script pointed at reflow2's own files, which generalised to nobody. Found by writing the assertion and watching it FAIL, not by reasoning.
  Fixed at the root rather than special-cased for `audience`, which is what makes one change serve every optional field in every project: `Capability.inputs`/`outputs`/`capability_type` (0 of 170), `ChangeEvent.subject`, `Fragment.*`, the five never-set timestamps.
  THE WITHHOLDING DECISION WAS KEPT. The names ride the flat list that was already behind `include_unused`; the default reply grew by ONE figure per domain (`domains[].properties`), never by a wall of names. Extending the withheld list was the only shape that could close the hole without re-creating the noise the fourth decision measured.
  EDGE PROPERTIES CAME TOO, on the same walk that already had the edges in hand (`GOVERNED_BY.ruling` was 0 of 912 and nothing shipped could say so), reported as a second figure so the vacuous-zero rule stays visible.
  🛑 HONEST LIMIT, PINNED BY A TEST: a property carrying a schema DEFAULT can never be named unused, because the store materialises defaults on write and every instance carries one. What this names is the UNDEFAULTED optional — which is the class that matters precisely because `req:defaults-do-not-assert` is why the fields worth asking about have no default. And the naming is REPORTABLE rather than REPORTED: it arrives only when somebody asks for the list.
properties.name: A design reports which of the vocabulary it has never used, grouped by domain, parkable, with the list on request
